chunks: What the Shaykh — may Allah the Exalted support him — informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl and ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Madāʾinī, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said:
Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام was asked about a man who slaughtered a bird, and its blood fell into the well, so he said:

“Buckets are to be drawn from it. This is when it has been slaughtered properly; then it is like this. As for anything else that falls into the well of water and dies in it: the greatest of it is the human being, from which seventy buckets are drawn; and the least of it is the sparrow, from which one bucket is drawn; and what is besides that is between these two.”

Then he said — may Allah the Exalted support him: if a donkey, a cow, a horse, or similar beasts dies in it, and the water has not changed due to its death, then one kurr of water is to be drawn from it; and if the water is less than that, all of it is to be drawn out.

key_terms.الدَّوَابِّ: beasts or riding animals such as donkey, cow, and horse
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well into which impurity falls
key_terms.الْعُصْفُورُ: the sparrow, cited as the smallest example in the ruling
key_terms.بِدَمِهِ: with its blood; referring to the blood of the slaughtered bird entering the well
key_terms.ذَكِيًّا: properly slaughtered according to legal requirements
key_terms.سَبْعُونَ دَلْوًا: the prescribed amount of seventy buckets in the case of the human being
key_terms.كُرٌّ: a kurr; a large prescribed quantity of water
key_terms.يُنْزَحُ: water is drawn out from the well for purification

ai.seo_question: How much water must be drawn from a well if blood or a dead animal falls into it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings on purifying well water when blood or dead animals fall into it. It specifies different amounts of water to be drawn depending on what fell into the well, indicating graded rulings in matters of najasah and taharah. It is significant in Shiʿi fiqh for the jurisprudence of water purification.
